Make it feel like you're talking TO him, not writing ABOUT him. Also, connect yourself to him: end with 'Fellow Island Hopper' instead of formal sign-off. The key shift: imagine you're actually going to print this and mail it (which you should! Here's his contact: wimpykid.com/contact). Start with your high school misconception: 'Entering high school, I thought success meant perfect grades and solitary achievement. I was too shy to see value in connections.' Then pivot to your transformation: 'Four years later, I know the truth - success is the network you build.' Define YOUR successful college: 'Meeting as many people as possible, because the whole value of college is the people you meet - professors who become mentors, peers who become collaborators.' Add specific CMU elements but don't overdo it - mention a club or two but keep it universal. Include your secondary insight: 'adopting new interests like rediscovering reading for pleasure after years of assigned texts.' Connect to your teaching philosophy: 'Learning doesn't just come from classrooms but from conversations, collaborations, late-night debugging sessions with friends.' End with forward-looking: 'I'm most excited not about what I'll learn, but WHO I'll learn it with and from.'
